claim: Roger Bannister was the first person to run a mile in under four minutes.

heard.quote: On 6 May 1954, the English athlete Roger Bannister became the first man ever to achieve a sub-four-minute mile.

heard.who: EBSCO Research Starters, entry on the four-minute mile
heard.quote: by becoming the first athlete to run a mile in less than 4 minutes.

answer: Yes. On 6 May 1954 Roger Bannister ran the mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds at the Iffley Road track in Oxford. Two team-mates, Chris Brasher and Chris Chataway, set the pace for him.

facts.text: On 6 May 1954 Roger Bannister ran the mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds at the Iffley Road track in Oxford, the first recorded mile under four minutes.

sources.title: First four-minute mile
sources.quote: Thereafter, Bannister threw in all his reserves and broke the tape in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds

sources.title: Bannister Beats the Four-Minute Mile
sources.quote: British runner Roger Bannister surpassed a significant milestone in track athletics by becoming the first athlete to run a mile in less than 4 minutes. His record time was 3 minutes, 59.4 seconds.

sources.title: First person to run a mile in less than four minutes
sources.quote: Running in front of a 3,000-strong crowd at Oxford University's Iffley Road track, the 25-year-old recorded a time of 3 min 59.4 sec

facts.text: Two team-mates, Chris Brasher and Chris Chataway, set the pace for Bannister during the race.

sources.title: Bannister Beats the Four-Minute Mile
sources.quote: he conferred with AAA teammates Chris Brasher and Christopher Chataway, who would serve as his pacesetters.

sources.title: A mile and a milestone - 50 years later
sources.quote: Brasher went into the lead for the first quarter of a mile and Chataway went into the lead near the three-quarter-mile mark.

sources.title: Roger Bannister's sub-four-minute mile, 70 years on
sources.quote: overtook the second of his pacemakers, Chris Chataway, and prepared to enter unchartered territory

contested.text: Because Bannister ran with pacemakers, some count his run as less of a lone feat. Bannister himself said he doubted he could have done it without them.

sources.title: A mile and a milestone - 50 years later
sources.quote: "Without the two Chrises to pace me, I don't believe I could have done what I did,"

could_not_verify: Whether any earlier unrecorded run beat four minutes: the sources only speak of the first recorded one.
A World Athletics or Amateur Athletic Association ratification document for the 3:59.4 time.
not_claimed: That Bannister ran alone or unpaced.
That his time was the fastest mile ever; it did not stand as the record for long.
